svg.title: TOPAK I4 — FloorRouting.tla: a floor that permits anything its predecessor did not is never deployed without an anchor issuance, and the deployed floor never permits everything. Two invariants, each with the mutation that breaks it: checked by TLC, proved by TLAPS and in Lean
svg.desc: The routing half of ADR-0030 §9's property check, drawn from the module's own text and from every results file about it, all read at build time: the router, the two properties, the mutation matrix, the witnesses, ADR-0030 §9's table compared row by row, every theorem and lemma, the certified run and the Lean re-encoding. A floor is modelled by its meaning, the set of requests it permits, over a three-request universe, and implication is inclusion: the module "checks the routing logic, not the analyzer" (its header), on the solver-trust assumption ADR-0030 states. Nothing here is said of the reference. The module is frozen, cited by digest (ADR-0030 §9, ADR-0046, ADR-0053).

"A proved obligation is a theorem of the module under its assumptions and the hypotheses the statement names; the prover, not the constants, bounds the claim. Mutations and witnesses are behaviours and stay with TLC."

Every theorem here takes Mut = "none" as its hypothesis, where Seats_proof.tla and FloorComposition_proof.tla take only the mutations that break each property: each property is proved unmutated, and not shown to survive the other mutation (the diagram's reading).
